name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,348

clue.text: Disregard poetry in Old English

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A reader skips over the poems in an anthology of Anglo-Saxon literature.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSE goes inside O...E. OVERSEE is used here in its old sense of overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee once meant to overlook, that is to fail to notice or ignore something, an older sense now rare.

clue.text: Additional seconds making a significant difference

blocks.note: odd can mean extra or spare, as in an odd sock or odd jobs
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A few extra seconds decided the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'it makes no odds' shows ODDS meaning a difference that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'what's the odds?' or 'makes no odds', the word means the gap or difference that counts.

clue.text: Drugs said to relax

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard spoken, so we want its sound not its spelling

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: Someone claims that taking drugs helps them unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or slacken off, making something less tense, so it matches relax as a verb.

clue.text: Defectors renouncing Germany released without suffering punishment

indicators.note: renouncing something means giving it up, so a letter is dropped from the word
released letters are set free to fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Spies who abandoned East Germany were set free without being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from DEFECTORS, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is an idiom for escaping penalty or harm entirely.

clue.text: Choose today to abandon girl at court

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a girl's name
CT is an abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone decides today to walk out on a girlfriend at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: ADELE at CT gives ADELECT; AD (the present era) leaves it, giving ELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to pick or decide on, a direct synonym of choose as a verb.

clue.text: Heads to restrict the use of tests at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before

blocks.note: to block something is to obstruct or restrict it
the final letter of tests

explanation.surface: Head teachers move to limit how much exams are used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like head teachers, but a block is slang for a head, as in 'knock your block off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Block is informal slang for a person's head, so the plural is heads.

clue.text: Record about to be overturned by German lumberjack

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned turns a word upside down so it reads the other way

blocks.note: a log is a written record
G is an abbreviation for German
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A record is about to be broken by a German athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' works on 'about' only; 'record' and 'German' stay as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A logger is someone who fells trees for timber, which is what a lumberjack does.

clue.text: Girl working to replace caveat at the end of agreement

indicators.note: replacing one thing with another swaps a letter out for new ones
the end of a word points to its final letter

blocks.note: a girl's name
a machine that is on is working
the final letter of caveat

explanation.surface: A girl at work drops the warning clause at the end of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: In CONSTANCE, the T is swapped for ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonance means harmony or accord between things, so it is a formal synonym of agreement.

clue.text: Stop when lad with new stilts takes a tumble

indicators.note: something that tumbles falls in a jumble, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is an abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy on new stilts falls over and everything halts.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where all movement ceases, so it is a noun meaning stop.

clue.text: Find out when heads of international schools convene in town

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of the words that follow
meeting in a town places them inside its name

blocks.note: Dover is a port town in Kent, England
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Delegates discover something when school leaders hold a conference in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to learn or come upon something previously unknown, which is to find out.

clue.text: A country's united by the dissemination of biased information? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only part of the word is kept, its first half dropped

blocks.note: U is an abbreviation for united
spreading slanted information is propaganda

explanation.surface: A nation is held together by spreading slanted news, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' means only the back half of the long word survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African nation, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Rubbish produced by Whistler? Source of inspiration's first to go

indicators.note: the first letter is told to leave, so it drops off the front of the word

blocks.note: a referee blows a whistle
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a Whistler painting as rubbish, made after the artist lost his inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler looks like the painter James McNeill Whistler, but here is a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is waste material thrown away, a noun synonym of rubbish or trash.

clue.text: Fantastic offer Hector ultimately declined is not to be made public

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters are reshaped freely
ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of declined

explanation.surface: Hector turned down a fantastic offer, but that must stay secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made off the record is given confidentially and must not be published or quoted.

clue.text: Poor bear heard trapper's leader moving around

indicators.note: letters moving around shift places and settle in a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of trapper

explanation.surface: A wretched bear hears a hunter's chief prowling nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare means worn thin and shabby, so it is a sense of poor in quality or condition.

clue.text: American woman died after quarrel with son over a weapon

indicators.note: after places the word before it at the back, behind the pieces that follow
in a down entry over flips the word so it reads upward

blocks.note: broad is dated US slang for a woman
S is an abbreviation for son
a row is a quarrel
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An American woman died after a row with her son about a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Broad is dated American slang for a woman, and 'died after' sends D to the very end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy sword with a wide blade, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasant hordes run wild around Ohio

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of control, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for the US state Ohio

explanation.surface: Rampaging mobs rioting across Ohio make for a horrible scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run wild' reads as one phrase, but run is part of the letters and only wild does the mixing; 'around' just lets Ohio join in.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrendous means dreadful or shocking, an intensified way of saying very nasty.

clue.text: Miles overwhelmed by sorrow in front of knight's tomb

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it ends up inside the other word

blocks.note: dole is an archaic word for grief or sorrow
M is the abbreviation for miles
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A man named Miles, grief-stricken, stands before a knight's grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Dole in the sense of grief is archaic, found mostly in poetry and crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric megalithic structure of upright stones and a capstone, thought to be a burial chamber.

clue.text: Agreement not starting to produce an effect

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A treaty that never comes into force achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug or policy that acts has an effect or works, as in 'the medicine began to act'.

clue.text: Guardiola communicates confidence boosters

blocks.note: Pep Guardiola is the Spanish football manager
to talk is to communicate

explanation.surface: Football manager Pep Guardiola gives his players motivating speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep talks are short rousing speeches meant to encourage people and lift their morale.

clue.text: Time fuse eventually found by soldiers

indicators.note: eventually points to what comes in the end, the last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of fuse
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: Soldiers finally locate the time fuse on a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, so it is a span of time.

clue.text: Smutty writer about to face the Italian censor

blocks.note: a blue joke is a smutty one
a pen writes
C stands for circa, about
il is 'the' in Italian

explanation.surface: An author of dirty books is about to face the Italian censor.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to cut or edit out material, from the blue pencil editors once used to strike text.

clue.text: Dishonest fellow ejected from amusement park

indicators.note: something ejected is thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow
a funfair is a travelling amusement park

explanation.surface: A crooked man is thrown out of a theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishonest fellow' reads as one phrase, but fellow belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means not just or not honest in dealing, as in unfair play or practices.

clue.text: Titian's greed stupidly causing break up

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Renaissance painter Titian's greed foolishly wrecks a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to fall to pieces or come apart, matching the verb break up.

clue.text: Hastily mend top of net after game at university

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter
after puts the piece before it behind the piece that follows

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
the first letter of net
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: After a match at college, someone quickly repairs the top of the goal net.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is British usage for attending.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up clothes is to sew or make them quickly, so the phrase means to stitch hastily.

clue.text: Swelling with pride ultimately after last one's left

indicators.note: one having left means it has gone away, so that letter is taken out
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to stay is to last or endure
a is one
the final letter of pride

explanation.surface: Someone is puffed up with pride after the last person goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so it is one specific kind of swelling.

clue.text: Sharp practice finally admitted by Livingstone

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
something admitted is let inside, so it goes within the other word

blocks.note: Ken Livingstone was a former Mayor of London
the final letter of practice

explanation.surface: A sharp political trick is admitted by Livingstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone suggests the explorer David, but it is the London politician Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade or keen mind is sharp, so the adjective is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Monk in retreat accepting gold is unconcerned with right or wrong

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word reads the other way
accepting something means taking it in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A monk on a spiritual retreat takes a bribe of gold and has no scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' looks like a monastery retreat, but it turns the monk backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone lacking any moral sense at all, neither good nor bad by choice.

clue.text: Foreign article includes material showing what exotic dancers do

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb

indicators.note: a word that includes another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: une is the French indefinite article
cloth is fabric material

explanation.surface: An imported item of clothing reveals what striptease artists do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of clothing, but it is the grammatical word, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe is to remove garments, which strippers do as their act.

clue.text: Bear is close to river

blocks.note: a close is an end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A bear lives near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure something is to tolerate or put up with it, the verb sense of bear.

clue.text: Gate money essentially to go with Bill

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its middle letter

blocks.note: a bill is a printed notice, a poster
the middle letter of money

explanation.surface: Takings at the gate are essentially destined for Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate money' reads as a single phrase, ticket receipts, but the clue splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, especially a small one in a castle wall.
